articleTitle: Optical vector network analyzer based on optical single-sideband modulation
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical vector network analyzer (OVNA) based on optical single-sideband (OSSB) modulation can measure phase and magnitude responses of an optical device with sub-MHz resolution. To reduce the measurement error caused by the high-order sidebands in the OSSB modulation schemes, a theoretical analysis is performed and an OSSB modulation scheme based on 120-degree hybrid coupler is proposed. A novel OVNA is also proposed to enable the OSSB-based OVNA for measuring both the bandstop and bandpass devices. In addition, the OSSB-based OVNA is successfully applied to measure the phase and magnitude responses of the stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in optical fibers and a FBG sensor.

articleTitle: Physical-layer network coding in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Physical-Layer Network Coding (PNC) is a promising technique to improve the network throughput of full-duplex transmission in a wireless two-way relay channel. Here, we explore the application of PNC in optical systems and networks. Two transmitted optical signal frames are simply added together to form an optical PNC-coded composite frame, which shares the same network channel/resource. At their destined node, the composite signal is directly-detected, before being decoded by subtracting one of the two transmitted signal frames, which is either already known or stored locally, from the received PNC-coded composite frame.

articleTitle: Fiber senor for long-range and biomedical measurements
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we summarize our recent research work on two types of optical fiber sensors: long distance sensor and biomedical sensor. For long distance sensing, we demonstrated our 150-km long distance fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) temperature and vibration sensor system and Brillouin optical time domain analysis distributed sensor system. For biomedical sensing, we demonstrated our microbend fiber sensors for measurements of breathing rate/heat rate and Ballistocardiogram waveform. A new sensor for patient's breathing measurement by using fiber loop ringdown spectroscopy is also introduced.

articleTitle: A special spun birefringent fiber optic current sensor
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A special spun linear birefringent fiber was designed and achieved for the fiber optic current sensor (FOCS) based on polarization-rotated reflection interferometers. In contrast with conventional sensing fibers used in FOCS the fiber integrates a function of a quarter wave plate. A fiber optic current sensor based on the spun fiber was constructed, and its performance was tested. The sensor output has a good linearity performance in a wide range of current. (10 to 5000Arms). The ratio error is within ±0.1% and the phase error is within ±2 min at a rated AC current of 1000Arms. The sensor could be used for current measuring in the electric power industry and the electrowinning industry.

articleTitle: Multi-octave operation of analog optical link using parallel intensity modulators
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we show in detail that the complementary modulation characteristic of the parallel intensity Mach-Zehnder modulators can be exploited for the cancellation of the second order harmonic distortion in the analog optical links. A suppression of 29.3 dB in the second order harmonic distortion is experimentally demonstrated. By using this proposed technique, multi-octave operation of the link is implemented. The proposed approach can be used to suppress the second order harmonic distortion which is pronounced in the low biased links. This technique shows excellent potential for future multi-octave analog optical links.

articleTitle: Constant envelope modulation enabled fiber nonlinearity mitigation for CO-OFDM transmissions
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an approach based on constant envelope modulation to mitigate fiber induced nonlinearities in CO-OFDM systems. The extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only greatly mitigates the nonlinear sensitivity of CO-OFDM transmissions but also avoids the severe nonlinear tolerance degradation caused by inline dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Cost-effective and green TDM-PON scheme with OFDM downstream and SCFDE upstream for next-generation access network
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a hybrid TDM-PON scheme with orthogonal frequency division multiple (OFDM) downstream and single-carrier frequency domain equalization (SCFDE) upstream to achieve low-complexity and green access. Upstream and downstream 26.7km and point-to-point 83.7km standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) transmissions were demonstrated to verify its feasibility.

articleTitle: Phase noise estimation based on direct detection using phase noise to intensity noise conversion
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a method to estimate the laser phase noise using the phase noise to intensity noise conversion based on the direct detection (DD) technique. It is shown by simulation that the estimated results approach when the laser line-width is no larger than 1MHz. Besides, compared with coherent detection -based phase noise estimation, the DD technique provides cost-efficient solutions.

articleTitle: Throughput model for IEEE 802.11 distributed coordination function in radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we present an analytical model to evaluate the throughput of IEEE 802.11 distributed coordination function in radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna systems where multiple remote antenna units are connected to one access point by different-length fiber links. In the model, the unequal delay induced by different fiber length is involved with the consideration of mutual HN problems. The derived model shows good agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of cyclic arrayed waveguide grating with distributed waveguide directions for uniform loss
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel method to achieve cyclic arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) router with uniform channel insertion loss over the entire free spectral range (FSR). By appropriately distributing the pointing directions of the arrayed waveguides at the output star coupler to the entire output waveguide array instead of the central output alone in conventional design, the optical energy of different wavelengths can be uniformly distributed to different output waveguides. The simulation results show that such a design can substantially reduce the channel insertion loss nonuniformity from 3dB to less than 1 dB.

articleTitle: A tnnable electro-optic microwave photonic filter based on photonic crystal for 60GHz radio over fiber system
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tunable microwave photonic filter (MPF) employing dynamic modulation based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) is presented. With low group velocity and low loss photonic crystal structure, the novel MPF with a length about 50 μm is proposed for 60-GHz ROF system. The modulation sensitivities are about 45/V for group index, 22.5GHz/V for free spectral range (FSR), while the device size is only 1.21% as the traditional fiber ring resonator. The extinction ratio of the MPF is about 10 dB, along with the 4.02GHz 3dB bandwidth, and the requirement of received data's signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can be reduced by 9 dB for the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> bit-error ratio (BER).

articleTitle: Fiber-optic acoustic and pressure sensors with ultra-high sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Pressure/acoustic sensors based on a hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber (HC-PBF) with thin outer-cladding and a fiber-tip micro-cavity with ultra-thin graphene diaphragm are reported. The HC-PBF sensor demonstrates a normalized acoustic responsivity of ~25 dB higher than standard single mode fiber while the fiber-tip sensor has a record high pressure responsivity of well over 1000 nm/kPa.

articleTitle: UWB-over-fiber sensor network for accurate localization based on optical time-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An impulse radio (IR) ultra-wideband (UWB) over fiber sensor network for accurate localization based on optical time-division multiplexing (OTDM) is proposed and demonstrated. Neither clock synchronization nor parameter estimation is required in the proposed UWB sensor nodes. All complex signal processing is completed in the central station, which can greatly improve the localization accuracy and simplify the UWB sensor system. A proof-of-concept experiment is carried out. Two-dimension localization with centimeter-level spatial resolution is achieved.

articleTitle: A sensitive bi-reflection surface plasmon resonance waveguide sensor based on SiON
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-performance bi-reflection surface plasmon resonance waveguide sensor based on SiON was proposed. The thickness of Ag is optimized. The detection limit and the sensitivity are improved at the expense of loss using two planar reflection surfaces. A sensitivity of 103.8degree/RIU or 2.86×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>dB/RIU as well as a refractive index variation of 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>RIU were measured.

articleTitle: Optical modulation and detection based on a PN junction embedded silicon waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A carrier-depletion-based silicon MZ modulator is used for high-speed optical detection by leveraging the defect mediated absorption. As a modulator, the device exhibits a modulation efficiency of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub>L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub>=1.2 V.cm while as a detector, the responsivity is 22 mA/W at a reverse bias of-7.1 V. An operation speed of 35 Gb/s is obtained for both optical modulation and detection.

articleTitle: Time-delay signatures in chaotic semiconductor ring lasers with cross mutual injection
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The time-delay (TD) signatures of chaos in semiconductor ring lasers with cross mutual injection are investigated numerically. The TD signature is quantified via auto-correlation function. The injection parameter regions contributing to successful TD concealment are identified. It is shown that, higher injection strengths can be utilized for larger frequency detuning to achieve TD concealment, and the region contributing TD concealment exhibits V type in the parameter space. The chaotic SRL with TD signature suppression is highly desirable for chaotic communication systems and high speed random number generators integrated on photonic integrated circuit.

articleTitle: A numerical study of ring fibre for high capacity orbital angular momentum mode transmission
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we study the maximum number of orthogonal azimuthal orbital angular momentum modes that can be supported by ring fibres while maintaining a radial single-mode profile. We demonstrate that a ring fibre within the standard communications fibre dimensions can support up to ± 52nd order OAM modes.

articleTitle: Optical-frequency-comb-based broadband radio frequency channelization
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a photonic-assisted broadband radio frequency (RF) channelization scheme based on dual coherent optical frequency combs (OFCs). The advantages include coarse optical alignment requirement, ideal rectangular frequency response in each channel without any ultra-narrow optical filters, and digitalized output for further processing. System performance and key issues will be discussed.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion monitoring using four wave mixing of semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate an all-optical on-line chromatic dispersion (CD) monitoring technique for 40 Gbit/s return-to-zero on-off-keying (RZ-OOK) signal using the four wave mixing (FWM) effect of semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA). The received signal, whose carrier frequency is suppressed by a fiber bragg grating (FBG), is launched into the SOA together with a continuous wave. The optical power of one idle wave is considered to be the autocorrelation of the signal's sideband and used for CD monitoring. The CD up to 90 ps/nm is monitored for the RZ signal, and the effects of the polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and wavelength misalignment are also discussed and experimentally investigated. This scheme requires neither modification at transmitter nor complicated digital signal processing at receiver. Furthermore, it is operated in all-optical, and has the potential to be applied to the higher speed system with optical time division multiplexed (OTDM) technique.

articleTitle: Broadband downlink stable radio frequency phase delivery exploiting fiber chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a broadband phase compensation method for transfer radio frequency (RF) signal from remote antenna to center station through a radio-over-fiber (ROF) link. By exploiting fiber's chromatic dispersion, a calibration signal modulated on a computer-controlled tunable laser from the center is used for link-length compensation, a broadband frequency independent stabilized ROF link is fulfilled. A proof-of-concept experiment is carried out. Radio frequency was transferred 10 km and a phase fluctuation compression factor greater than 30 is achieved for 1205 MHz in 3000 seconds and for 2460 MHz in 5000 seconds.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband microwave-photonic chaotic radar for remote ranging
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A UWB microwave-photonic chaotic radar system for remote ranging is proposed and demonstrated. The chaotic detection signal is transmitted by an ultra-wideband transmitting antenna after a 24 km single-mode fiber transmission to a remote antenna unit. The received signal is converted into the corresponding optical signal through directly modulating and carried by another approximately 24 km single mode fiber back to the central station. The target detection and ranging are accomplished through cross correlation at the central station. Chaotic signals with bandwidths more than 18 GHz are generated experimentally. Ranging of single-target and double-target is demonstrated. The system can not only implement the remote control of the radar, but also has a high range resolution.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensitivity of the tilt long-period fiber gratings coated with nano-scale golden film
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel class of tilt long-period fiber gratings (TLPFGs) coated with nano-scale gold film is introduced, which is at period of 368pm and easy to fabricate. Gold film at nano-scale has been deposited on TLPGs by adopting evaporation technique in Vacuum Film-Sputtering Machine. The experiment results demonstrate that the refractive index sensitivity measured by resonant wavelength shift is raised in the range of 1.441 to 1.475 with outer refractive index change, and the sensitivity measured by contrast is enhanced from -17.35dB/RIU to -57.55dB/RIU in the range of 1.392 to 1.441 with good correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of multi-user direct sequence spread spectrum system based on m sub-sequence
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the generating principle of m sub-sequence is introduced and analyzed. On this basis, a multi-user direct sequence spread spectrum(DSSS) communication system is constructed and simulated in Matlab. Simulation results show that the bit error rate(BER) of DSSS communication using m sub-sequences as spreading codes is not inferior to the system using m sequences and gold sequences. It can be proved that the m sub-sequences have good anti-interference ability, and can be used in communication system.

articleTitle: Passively Q-switched linear-cavity erbium-doped fiber laser based on graphene saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a passively Q-switched erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) based on graphene as a saturable absorber (SA). Two fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) are used as the end mirrors in an all-fiber linear cavity. The Q-switched EDFL has a pump threshold of 68.2 mW. The minimum pulse duration is 0.85 μs and the highest pulse energy is 40.9 nJ. The pulse repetition rate of the fiber laser can be widely changed from 51.1 to 118.1 kHz by increasing the pump power from 68.2 to 400 mW.

articleTitle: EBG ME-dipole antenna with enhanced gain for intelligent radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An electromagnetic band-gad (ERG) magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with enhanced gain is proposed for intelligent radio-over-fiber systems. With the ERG etched around the radiator patch, gain enhancement is achieved without deteriorating the previous impedance bandwidth of more than 33% from 50 to 70 GHz. The maximum gain is increased from 7.7 to 11.7 dBi. Many advantages, such as low cost, easy fabrication, wide bandwidth and high gain are presented.

articleTitle: Radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna systems supporting IEEE 802.11N/AC standards
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna systems promise to provide broadband indoor wireless coverage with transparency to radio communication standards and operating bands. The IEEE802.11n/ac standards approved recently with new technological features bring about a set of challenges and issues to the radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna systems, which are addressed and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: An energy-efficient mechanism of passive optical access network based on Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ethernet Passive Optical Network (EPON) as a new type of access network technology has been applied to the LAN and core network. Its energy saving efficiency will not only directly affect the performance of the network, but also will restrict the development of environment. This paper proposes a new type of energy efficient mechanism which takes all factors such as the traffic of OLT(Optical Line Terminal) and the traffic of ONU(Optical Network Unit) into consideration, and applies mathematical ideas about classified discussion to distribute the uplink TS(time-slot) to ONUs on the basis of the original structure. So as to make the sleep time of system is the most reasonable and the QoS (Quality of Service) is satisfied as well.

articleTitle: Recent advances in ultrafast all-optical signal processing and generation
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reviews our recent works on all-optical processing and generation of ultrafast signals down to the sub-picosecond regime based on linear optical filters such as directional coupler, integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer and long period gratings.

Author Keywords: Photonics differentiator; Linear optical filtering techniques

articleTitle: Dual-frequency indoor location scheme by combining WLAN and RFID in radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-frequency location scheme combining WLAN and RFID signals at different frequency bands to conduct indoor location together in radio-over-fiber (RoF) systems. Using dual-frequency method, the wallboard attenuation can be estimated more accurately. In particular, we propose three procedures for wallboard auto-detection and free-space propagation model calibration which perform a high-accuracy indoor location function.

articleTitle: An optically tunable optoelectronic oscillator incorparating a bandpass microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have proposed an optically tunable optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) incorporating a single passband microwave photonic filter (MPF) based on an electro-optic phase modulator and a Fabry-Pérot semiconductor optical amplifier (FP-SOA). By replacing the electrical bandpass filter in a traditional single-loop OEO with the MPF, the oscillating frequency can be simply tuned by altering the bias current of the FP-SOA.

articleTitle: Multiple basestation RoF system enabled by multiple wavelength conversion based on polarization multiplexed FWM in SOA
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An approach for multiple-frequency millimeter-wave (mm-wave) signal generation is proposed for radio-over-fiber (RoF) systems with multiple base stations (MBSs). Two groups of orthogonally polarized pumps are injected into a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA), and subsequently, ten new different wavelengths are generated via four-wave mixing (FWM). At the BSs, different wavelengths are filtered out using de-multiplexer and then input to a photo-diode (PD) to generate mm-wave signals with the frequencies of 52-68 GHz which have 2 GHz grid. Simulation results verify that the proposed multiple wavelength conversion enhanced MBS-RoF system can work properly.

articleTitle: High-frequency mode-beating in distributed feedback laser with a semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A monolithic semiconductor laser, which can generate high frequency mode-beating over 100GHz, is reported. This laser employs a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) as the integrated feedback cavity of a complex-coupled distributed feedback laser (DFB). Stable dual-mode emission, with low strength difference is demonstrated. Mode-beating frequency of this laser can be tuned from 87.41 to 103.64 GHz, when the currents injected into each laser section are adjusted. In all frequency range, the strength difference of two main modes is smaller than 10 dB and the strength of the other side mode is 20 dB lower than the two main modes.

articleTitle: Microwave spectrum sensing based on photonic time stretch with a large stretch factor
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a microwave spectrum sensing system based on photonic time stretch with large stretch factor beyond 80 is designed and experimentally demonstrated. A 10 GHz input signal is turned into a 122 MHz signal after stretching and the signal spectrum is successfully reconstructed by a DSP. The mean square error for spectrum sensing of X-band microwave signal in the experiment is measured to be 0.34 MHz.

articleTitle: Photonic generation of millimeter-wave signals with eighteen multiplied frequency using cascaded FWM in a single SOA
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel technique for eighteen multiplied frequency is proposed and investigated based on an intensity modulator and cascaded four-wave-mixing (FWM) effects in a single semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA). The results show that the 36-GHz and 90-GHz millimeter waves are achieved when the input frequencies are 2-GHz and 5GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Optical generation of microwave carrier using optically injection-locked fabry-perot laser diodes in tandem
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrated an optical generation of microwave carrier using optically injection-locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes in tandem through a phase modulator. It is verified that the proposed scheme is able to achieve an optical carrier suppressed (OCS) signal with a good suppression ratio simultaneously through a programmable optical filter and by use of optical injection locking technique. The generated microwave carrier at 60-GHz with baseband data is down converted to baseband signal to be characterized.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable optical filters using self-coupled optical waveguide (SCOW) resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report our recent progress on reconfigurable self-coupled optical waveguide (SCOW) resonators as optical filters. The SCOW resonators exhibit high-order optical filtering features with less strict requirement on device fabrication as required in regular coupled microring filters.

articleTitle: A novel sampling Bragg grating for DFB laser
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on reconstruction equivalent chirp (REC) technology, we propose a special structure for distributed feed-back (DFB) lasers realized by changing the duty cycle of one side in sampling Bragg grating, thus the equivalent apodization is introduced in this side, resulting into the magnitude of the equivalent index modulation is varied and smaller than the other side. As a conventional equivalent π phase-shift sampling Bragg grating (SBG), this proposed structure also introduces an equivalent π phase-shift into both its ±1 storder channel. Combined with the conventional equivalent π phase-shift, the sampling technique can be used to design and fabricate Semiconductor or fiber lasers conveniently.

articleTitle: Recent progress in random fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reviews recent progress in random fiber lasers (RFLs), including fundamental studies on their physical characteristics, design and analysis, as well as their applications, i.e., novel lasers, sensing, and amphfication indicating that RFLs would have an impact on Fiber Optics. Furthermore, the research progress in RFLs at University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) is presented.

articleTitle: Experimental verification platform for FC-over-WDM-based avionic network
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fibre Channel has been deployed on a number of military/aerospace platforms such as, F35/JSF, F8, F16, E2C, etc. Owing to the incomparable performance of wavelength division multiplexing (WDM), advanced optical networks with WDM have been targeted as the technology of choice to realize the desired avionic network of the future. The combination of FC with WDM is expected to play an important role in optimizing avionic system. This paper studies the feasibility of FC over WDM with an experiment verification platform. Test results with high transmission rate and good performance indicates that FC over WDM can be applied effectively in avionics environment and is a good choice for the further research of WDM technology under avionics environment.

articleTitle: Optical 90° hybrid based on silicon-on-insulator 4×4 multimode interference coupler for integrated coherent receiver application
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical 90° hybrid based on Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) 4×4 multimode interference(MMI) coupler is designed and simulated for the application of integrated coherent receiver(ICR). The beam propagation method(BPM) is used to verify the performance of the device. The 4×4 MMI coupler show good performance over C-band of TM mode with wavelength dependent loss(WDL) <;0.3 dB, output power imbalance <;0.35dB, phase error better than 2°.

articleTitle: Study on remodulation scheme based on a two-section reflective semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple and cost effective remodulation scheme based on a single two-section RSOA is proposed. In the two-section RSOA, the first section is served as a modulator to upload upstream signal and the second section works as an optical squeezer to effectively erase downstream data. The upstream performance dependence on the structural and operating parameters is investigated. The results show that the output upstream signal quality can be effectively improved by optimizing these parameters.

articleTitle: A numerical study of UTC-PD structures with berylium as the p-dopant
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically investigate UTC PD structures that use highly diffusible beryllium (Be) as the p-type impurity in absorption layer An intrinsic InGaAs layer is added between the absorption layer and collection layer as a diffusion buffer. The influence of this buffer layer is analyzed, and the results obtain shows that high responsivity and high speed can be achieved.

articleTitle: Tropospheric error correction in passive location systems based distributed fiber sensor array
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy in near-field passive location systems that are based on distributed fiber sensor array, we propose a method to correct the tropospheric error The method utilizes the Hopfield refractivity profile model for the near-filed targets. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm could quickly converge with improved precision.

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission of optical vortex beams at a dielectric interface
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper discusses the paraxial vortex beams (Laguerre-Gaussian modes) incident on a homogeneous, isotropic and lossless dielectric plane. Using Fourier transform, vortex beams are decomposed into plane waves and then multiplied by the Fresnel coefficients. The reflected or transmitted vortex beams can be obtained via inverse Fourier transformation. The results show that the centre of the intensity gravity for both reflection and transmission of light beams undergoes a transverse shift. In particular, the intensity distribution of the transmitted beam is similar to that of diagonal Hermite-Gaussian beams.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated 10-channel-selectable light sources fabricated by SAG technology
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A monolithic integration of ten 1.5-μm range InGaAsP/InP distributed feedback lasers with 10×1 multimode-interference (MMI) optical combiner using the selective area growth technology is proposed and demonstrated. Our design of selectable light sources with selective area growth (SAG) technology can be fabricated easily, which is promising for obtaining low cost and high-yield multi-wavelength light sources.

articleTitle: Beyond 100 Gb/s: Advanced DSP techniques enabling high spectral efficiency and flexible optical communications
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Coherent optical communications leveraged the fundamental philosophies and building blocks of mature wireless/copper-wire DSP technologies and has been a huge success with polarization-multiplexed QPSK at 100Gb/s per channel transponders currently in wide deployments. We discuss on further advances in DSP techniques to enable single-carrier transmission approaching 1 Tb/s as well as software-defined flexible transponders supporting adaptive modulation formats and elastic optical networks.

articleTitle: A study on the measurement error of the optical vector network analyzer based on single-sideband modulation
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A comprehensive study of the optical single-sideband (OSSB) modulation based optical vector network analyzer (OVNA) is performed to reveal the origination of the measurement error. By applying stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in an 8-km single-mode fiber (SMF) as the device-under-test (DUT), and employing an optical processor to control the high-order sidebands of the OSSB signal, numerical simulation and experiment results indicate that the +2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order sideband introduces the major measurement error, which should be suppressed to improve the accuracy of the measurement.

articleTitle: Ultra compact cross-order AWG triplexer based on SU-8 polymer
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact arrayed waveguide grating triplexer based on small SU-8 strip waveguides is designed by using cross-order method. The AWG triplexer has a very compact size of as small as 1.3 × 0.402 mm2 since the high index contrast between SU-8 core layer and SiO2 and air cladding, and can be easily fabricated by using direct ultraviolet photolithography process without additional etching process. The simulation results show that the 3-dB bandwidths of three channels (1310nm, 1490nm and 1550nm) for TE polarization are greater than 11 nm and each channel has a low polarization dependence wavelength shift less than 0.65nm.

articleTitle: Multiwavelength narrow linewidth erbium-doped fiber laser based on cascading two FP-LDs
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and demonstrate a technique to realize multiwavelength operation in an erbium-dopedfiber laser (EDFL) by inserting two Fabry Pérot laser diodes (FP-LDs) in the laser cavity in cascaded way. The FP-LDs not only act as wavelength selection elements, but also offer optical gain or loss for the operation wavelengths in the laser cavity. The gains or losses for the oscillation wavelengths obtained from FP-LDs differ with adjustment of the driving current of the FP-LDs. Thus, the utilization of the FP-LDs in the laser cavity can introduce wavelength dependent gain or loss which can effectively suppress the competition caused by the homogeneous gain broadening of the erbium-doped fiber (EDF). As a result, 16-wavelength operation with a wavelength-spacing of 1.25 nm has been achieved. The measured power fluctuation of each wavelength is smaller than 0.4dB. Furthermore, the injection locking of the FP-LDs ensures a narrow linewidth of the EDFL output and the linewidth is estimated to be narrower than 100 MHz.

articleTitle: An Erbium-doped fiber laser based on a 3×3 microfiber coupler
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple and compact Erbium-doped fiber laser is demonstrated with two Sagnac loops formed by a 3×3 microfiber coupler. By fusing two ports on each side of the 3 ×3 microfiber coupler and embedding a 90 cm Erbium-doped fiber in one loop, a stable laser output is achieved at 1530 nm region with an optical signal to noise ratio of ~40 dB using a 980-nm pump. Taking advantage of the large evanescent field and excellent temperature and mechanical properties of the micro-sized coupled area, the device has great potentials in tunable laser and active sensing for refractive index, temperature, strain and pressure.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast line scan microscopic imaging system
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The speed of line scan imaging system is limited either by scanning technique or the frame rate of CCD and CMOS cameras. By using hybrid dispersion laser scanning technique, we built an ultra-fast line scan microscopic imaging system with record frame rate of 1GHz. This technique is promising to be used for capturing fast process, especially non-repetitive transient phenomena.

articleTitle: Tunable and narrow linewidth RF signal generation based on dual-injection semiconductor ring laser
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An integrated optoelectronic device for the generation of tunable and narrow linewidth radio frequency (RF) signals is proposed, consisting of two DFB lasers that are external injected into a semiconductor ring laser (SRL). The three lasers achieve mutual injection and phase locking. The beating between the output optical spectral lines generates an electrical signal with narrow linewidth and high tunibility.

articleTitle: Multi-band RF spectral compression and inversion using optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a high-efficient photonic approach that can simultaneously down-convert, compress and invert the spectrum of multiband RF signal through coherently heterodyning the optic-carried multiband RF signal with a frequency carefully aligned optical frequency comb. A proof of concept experiment with dual band RF spectral manipulation is demonstrated to validate this proposal. Performance is also investigated that the system an EVM degradation of 7.5% compared to the back to back condition.

articleTitle: Optical attractive force in tapered Mach-Zehnder and Sagnac loop interferometers for active microsensing applications
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The optical attractive force can be available when the diameter of the tapered fiber is approaching the wavelength scale. By incorporating the tapered fiber into the micro fiber Mach-Zehnder and Sagnac loop interferometers, the optical attractive force can be employed to attract the desired micro- or nano-particles for active microsensing.

articleTitle: Photonic analog-to-digital conversion based on photonic time stretch and compressive sensing with optical random mixing
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An approach to realizing photonic analog-to-digital conversion based on photonic time stretch and compressive sensing (CS) technique is proposed. A multi-tone signal (spectrally sparse) within a 20 GHz bandwidth is investigated. The wideband signal is firstly stretched in the time domain by a photonic time-stretcher and then reconstructed by CS based on random demodulator (RD). The random mixing in RD is realized optically with a spatial light modulator (SLM). Thanks to the techniques of time stretch and CS, wideband spectrally-sparse signals can be acquired effectively with a sampling rate far below the Nyquist rate. A system with time stretch factor 10 and compression factor 8, which means a 1/80 of the Nyquist rate, is illustrated.

articleTitle: Optical waveguide ring based notch filter for microwave photonic signal processing
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical waveguide ring based notch filter was designed and fabricated with polymer PSQ-Ls for microwave photonic signal processing. The waveguide ring consists of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) as the tunable coupler and two micro-heaters as the thermal-optic phase shifters. The coupling states, over-, critical- and under-coupling, were obtained with the phase shifter on the arm of MZI and the maximum notch depth of about 18dB was achieved. The filtering frequency can also be tuned with the phase shifter on the ring waveguide. The notch filtering function to obtain single sideband RF signal was demonstrated experimentally with the polymer waveguide ring.

articleTitle: Three dimensional multifunctional nanomechanical photonic crystal sensor with high sensitivity by using pillar-inserted aslant nanocavity resonator
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method to detect nanomechanical variations in the three dimensional space with a shoulder-coupled pillar-inserted aslant photonic crystal nanocavity resonator. FEM and 3D-FDTD simulation software are employed to investigate the sensing characteristics. With high quality factor of the aslant nanocavity and the optimized structure, high sensitivity of nanomechanical sensing can be achieved in three dimensions and the limitation of the smallest detectable variations is ultra small. For its ultra small size and ultra high sensitivity in every dimension, this versatile nanomechanical sensor can be widely used in MEMS.

articleTitle: Duplex chaotic message tranmission using polarization mode carriers in small networks of three chaotic vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Duplex chaotic message transmission based on polarization mode carriers is investigated numerically in a small network consisting of three chaotic vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers. The results show that, under proper conditions, two messages at the speed of a few GHz can be encoded/decoded separately and successfully. The performance of the communication is evaluated by using the well-known eye diagram and Q-factor.

articleTitle: A real-time detection and self-control phase-sensitive OTDR distributed sensor system
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A real-time detection and self-control phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer (ϕ-OTDR) distributed sensor system is demonstrated. The system software can get the real-time data stream to detect the disturbance and self-control the Mach-Zehnder electro-optical modulator (MZEOM). In this way, the system can operate continuously and compensate the drift of the MZEOM automatically.

articleTitle: Dual wavelength semiconductor laser using asymmetric phase-shifts
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel dual wavelength semiconductor laser is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Stable dual wavelength lasing is established by the grating structure consisting of two asymmetric phase-shifts, which are distributed along the phase-arranging regions (PARs) in the sampling pattern. The wavelength spacing is about 0.51 nm corresponding to a beat signal about 64 GHz.

articleTitle: Optical millimeter-wave generation based on multiple modulations in an optical feedback loop
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple method to generate millimeter-wave signal is proposed and demonstrated. In our scheme, by configuring a multiple modulation loop, a wideband optical comb with good stability is obtained, and then the millimeter-wave signal is generated based on the beating in a high-speed photodetector of the optical carrier and the nth-order optical sideband filtered out by a Fabry-Perot filter. The experiments are demonstrated and 60 GHz millimeter wave with narrow linewidth is easily generated.

articleTitle: Pump-to-signal transfer improvement of fiber optical parametric amplifier with fiber Bragg grating reducing the first-order idler wave
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An approach to improve the pump-to-signal transfer efficiency of the fiber optical parametric amplifier (FOPA) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. A fiber Bragg grating (FBG) with the Bragg wavelength at 1550.1nm is introduced between two high nonlinear fibers (HNLFs) to reduce the first-order idler wave, which lead to the alteration of the relative power and relationships between the involved waves. And the output power of the signal is approximately 10dB increased compared with the absence of the FBG.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics of 1550nm VCSELs under external perturbations
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, nonlinear dynamical characteristics of 1550nm vertical-cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSELs) subject to positive optoelectronic feedback (POEF) or polarization-preserved optical feedback (PPOF) are experimentally investigated. For the case of POEF, various nonlinear dynamical behaviors including regular pulsing (RP), quasiperiodic pulsing (QP), chaotic pulsing (CP) and mode locking (ML) have been experimentally observed and a mapping of dynamical states is presented in the parameter space of bias current and feedback strength. For the case of PPF, the characteristics of this polarization switching (PS) between two orthogonal linearly polarized fundamental modes are strongly modified. The PPOF results in the PS point shift towards lower injection current, and the region within which the two polarization modes coexist is enlarged with the increase of the PPOF strength. Under too strong PPOF levels, the PS disappears.

Author Keywords: 1550 nm vertical-cavity surface emitting lasers (1550nm VCSELs)

articleTitle: A low-cost multi-wavelength laser based on hybrid integration technology for WDM-PON application
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A low-cost L-band multi-wavelength laser (MWL) is presented. The 16-channel laser with a wavelength spacing of 100GHz was fabricated in a hybrid method. This device can be applied into the broad access network based on fiber-to-the-home (FTTH). It consists of four 4-channel semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) arrays and an array waveguide grating (AWG) based on silica on silicon. 16-channel lasing operation is shown and the fiber-coupled output powers can reach up to 1.8mW while the threshold current is as low as 22mA. Direct modulation of the laser at 1.25GHz gives an open eye with an extinction ratio of 5.4dB.

articleTitle: Multi-wavelength Erbium-doped fiber laser with single mode fiber and high nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multi-wavelength Erbium-doped fiber (EDF) laser based on four-wave-mixing is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The 5km single mode fiber in the cavity enhances the four-wave-mixing to suppress the homogenous broadening of the erbium-doped fiber and get the stable multi-wavelength comb. The lasing stability is investigated. When the pump power is 300mW the fiber laser has 5-lasing lines and the maximum fluctuation of the output power is about 3.18dB. At the same time, a laser with 110m high nonlinear fiber (HNFL) is demonstrated. When the pump power is 300mW it has 7-lasing lines (above -30dBm) and the maximum fluctuation is 0.18dB.

articleTitle: Large bandgap shift by UV excimer laser induced quantum well intermixing for photonic integration
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A bandgap blue shift of 142nm with enhanced photoluminescence (PL), is demonstrated experimentally. in an InGaAsP/InP quantum well (QW) structure using KrF excimer laser induced quantum well intermixing (QWI) technique. The simple process only involves irradiation of UV pulses from a KrF excimer laser, followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) at 750 °C for 2 minutes. The absorption constant at the original band-edge is reduced to only 20dB/cm for the QWI waveguide. The fabricated QWI FP laser also has excellent optical and electrical properties, showing good potential for applications in monolithic integrated multibandgap devices.

articleTitle: Soliton coupling via group-velocity-matching cherenkov radiation in dispersion engineering fibers
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically present the group-velocity-matching Cherenkov radiation and the soliton spectral tunneling effect by using the concept of soliton coupling from a local state to the eigen state. A new wavelength conversion scheme with expanded wavelength span is proposed via cascaded soliton coupling by using two-segment fibers with three zero dispersion wavelengths. Numerical results show that energy conversion about 500 nm spanning can be realized.

Author Keywords: Soliton coupling Cascaded conversion Raman effect

articleTitle: Analysis of GE content in SiGe waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Silicon germanium (SiGe) is a completely miscible alloy with a lattice mismatch to the Si substrateof up to 4.17%, which has a lot of advantages, such as high refractive index, large electron mobility, compatibility with Si integrated circuit process, and so on. Based on the already established hundred nano-structure of SiGe ridge waveguide, effects of Ge content on effective refractive index and coupling efficiency characteristics are analyzed. Focus on the different losses in SiGe waveguide is analyzed. Through the optimization of Ge content, SiGe-OI optical waveguide has excellent losses characteristics at low Ge content.

articleTitle: Asymmetric property in the lasing spectrum of the phase-shifted distributed feedback laser with linearly chirped grating
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The phase-shifted distributed feedback (DFB) semiconductor laser with linearly chirped grating based on reconstruction equivalent chirp (REC) technique is theoretically analyzed and experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The asymmetric property of the lasing spectrum is analyzed according to the normalized threshold gain, and the different spectra from the rear and front side of the laser are compared. The fabricated laser has small lasing wavelength shift of 7pm/mA. It is the simplest way to realize chirped grating on semiconductor lasers to our knowledge.

articleTitle: LDPC-coded A×M-DAPPM systems for simulation of turbulent free-space optical communication system
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A LDPC coded DAPPM (4×4 & 4×8) modulated scheme for both strong and weak turbulent free-space optical communication is proposed and its BER performance is analyzed by Monte Carlo simulation. Results prove its well reliability especially for weak turbulent channel, and calls for advanced forward error control means to deal with strong turbulent channel.

articleTitle: Optimization of SOI wire waveguide geometry for maximum continuous wave Raman gain
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically investigated the relationship between the transverse waveguide geometry and the continuous-wave Raman gain in silicon-on-insulator wire waveguide Raman amplifiers. A Raman gain enhancement can be achieved in waveguides with small effective mode area.

articleTitle: Actively mode-locked fiber optical parametric oscillator based on feedback idler
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report an actively mode-locked fiber optical parametric oscillator (FOPO) based on feedback idler which is reflected by a fiber Bragg grating (FBG). The idler-resonant FOPO, configured in ring cavity, is based on high nonlinear fiber (HNLF) and the feedback idler which is modulated by a phase modulator (PM) is poured into the ring cavity via a 3-dB coupler pumped by a continuous wave (CW). With the PM activated and the cavity length synchronized, a stable train of 50 ps pulses can be obtained at a repetition rate of 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A compact microfiber coupler based Sagnac loop
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a compact Sagnac loop based on microfiber coupler which has a potential in application of laser, communication and sensing. As an example, a thermometer based on this structure is fabricated and shows a good temperature sensitivity.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing in a photonic link for acquisition of spectrally-sparse wideband signals: Potentials and limitations
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) is a novel technology to realize sub-Nyquist sampling for measuring of sparse signals. Due to the advantages of high bandwidth offered by photonics, realization of compressive sensing in a photonic link is of great interest. In this paper, we discussed the limitations of CS in a conventional photonic link A potential solution is proposed. To further reduce sampling rate, we propose to combine the techniques of photonic time stretch and CS. In addition, the photonic CS with random mixing realized by a spatial light modulator is discussed. Theoretical limit on frequency resolution for spectral mixing is derived.

articleTitle: Hybrid modulation for short range polymer optical fiber communications
publicationTitle: 2013 12th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to effectively exploit the spectrum of step-index polymer optical fiber (SI-POF) transmission system, a hybrid modulation format based on discrete multi-tone modulation (DMT) and M-ray Pulse Position Shift Keying (MPPSK) is proposed. The sideband interference component of the novel modulation schemes is analyzed. A new numerical symbols generating approach is introduced to strengthen the anti-interference capability of the system. Offline processing with arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) and digital storage oscilloscope (DSO) is adopted to investigate the transmission performance. A transmission rate of 510.5Mbps is achieved for 50m SI-POF in intensity modulated direct detection system. The experimental verification demonstrates that with the help of the new methodology an additional bit rate of 19.5 Mbps at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) region is obtained. Furthermore 6dB power is saved at a BER of 1× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>. Therefore, better spectrum efficiency can be achieved. The proposed modulation format combination can be also applied to other DMT and MPPSK over POF systems.
